name: Grimm
posts:
Want to try a Grimm one-shot, set in the Old West? [DAY, DATE] at [TIME], about 3 hours, on [Discord voice / the browser table].

Children are vanishing from a German colony on the plains, the colonists have a family they mean to hang for it, and the thing taking them is someone else. You'd be a Grimm marshal, a reformed Blutbad blacksmith, a Fuchsbau apothecary, a skeptical doctor, a Coyotl scout, a Ziegevolk gambler, or a Braucher.

It runs on rules I've been designing (3d6, roll low). Characters are ready-made and there's nothing to read. Afterward I'll ask a few quick questions about what worked. Interested?

**Grimm one-shot: The Larder at Hoffnungstal** 🐺
[DAY, DATE] · [TIME] · ~3 hours · voice
Ready-made characters, nothing to read, beginners welcome. Missing children, a lynch mob at the wrong door, and the Code of Swabia. React to grab a seat!
where: Friends and your regular group, by message.
Your own private Discord server, in a channel only invited people can see.
Invite them to the fan-games site first (it's locked to invited players), so they can open the creator and the Playtest page.
prep: Read The Larder at Hoffnungstal in the GM's Guide (Grimm creator → Guide tab → GM's Guide → Your first case). It's about two pages.
Open the creator's GM view and add the ready-made characters for as many players as you have (Table and characters → Add a ready-made character).
Online: start a shared table and have its link ready, or set up the dice bot in your Discord. In person: print the character sheets.
In the Discovery tab, prepare a diary discovery clock for the thing taking the children, with its threat clock; and have a Lynch mob clock (6) ready.
In Map and fight, check you can add a Wendigo (Konrad Weiss), a few Hired guns for the mob, and a Blutbad in full woge (Emil Raeber).
The day before: send everyone the time, the table link, and the Playtest page, your fan-games site, /playtest/. Tell them there's nothing to read.
Have a timer or clock in view. The run sheet below has the times.
cast: Grimm and Deputy U.S. Marshal. The law and the Code, in one person.
Blutbad blacksmith. Old Raeber ran with his pack.
Fuchsbau apothecary. Konrad's been buying a remedy for hunger.
Army surgeon. The torn dog's wounds bother him.
Coyotl scout. Has seen tracks that walk like a man.
Ziegevolk gambler. Konrad won big at cards, and Konrad never wins.
Braucher. Pastor Unruh brings the case to her door.
castNote: With fewer players, keep Lena (the hook) and Eliza or Gus (the mob and the Raebers). Silas or Roz leads them to the mill.
run: Pitch it in one breath: Wesen live hidden among us, and Grimms keep the old law between them and the rest of the world. Each player takes a character and reads their role and connection aloud. Explain only the roll: 3d6, at or under your number.
Pastor Unruh at Lena's door: three children gone, and the colony means to hang the Raebers. Go around: why does each of them ride out tonight?
Lanterns outside the Raeber land. Start the Lynch mob clock (6) and the threat clock. A Persuasion or Leadership roll pushes the mob back one for the night.

Old Raeber with a shotgun; Emil, who's been hunting it. Start the diary clock. Clues: the dog (Medicine), the frost-tracks (Tracking), the famine stories (Read People), the mill (Investigation, or Silas), Roz's ledger (Apothecary). Three clues are enough.
A Survival roll follows the tracks to the cold cellar under the mill race. Two children, alive. Whitlock and Roz keep them that way.
Skip the roll: Emil leads them there.
He comes home in woge: a Wendigo with the children's voices. The big fight, in a dark mill with flour in the air and fire close to hand.
The mob arrives with lanterns. Do they see the woge? Exposure, or Suspicion and a cover story. Eliza's badge against the Code.
